fields.title: Vision: what the world will look like if we succeed
fields.keyTakeaway: Vision describes changed human behavior, not future features. Its test is simple: does it help reject good ideas that don't lead to it?
fields.checkQuestion: How do you distinguish a vision from an advertising slogan?
fields.blocks/0/text: Key question of the node: **how will the company change the market?**
fields.blocks/1/text: **What happens if you don't answer the question.** Every new idea seems equally relevant. The product gets cluttered with capabilities that have no shared meaning, and three years later nobody can explain what it's for.
fields.blocks/2/items/0: **About people, not the product** — what will change in their behavior: "a person who used to drop books now finishes one a month."
fields.blocks/2/items/1: **It eliminates** — it must imply a "no" for some good ideas. A vision that agrees with everything is useless.
fields.blocks/2/items/2: **Beyond the planning horizon** — three to five years, otherwise it's a goal.
fields.blocks/2/items/3: **Slogan test:** if the sentence can be placed on a competitor's website unchanged, it is not a vision.
fields.blocks/3/text: **Product Evolution Canvas** helps lay out the path to a vision by stages: what must be true at each stage so the next becomes possible. This turns a distant picture into a sequence of testable states and shows which step you missed.
fields.blocks/4/text:
Vision: "a person who hasn't finished books in recent years reads regularly again — not because they forced themselves, but because they found a rhythm."

What follows from it:
yes — work on the first book, recommendations, short formats, rhythm;
no — chasing catalog size, even though it's an obvious idea and requested;
no — a social network around reading as a separate product until the first book issue is solved.

Stages: first, they finish the first book; then they come back for the second on their own; then they recommend to each other — and only here does social become meaningful.

It was this vision that stopped buying rights to new releases for half the annual budget.
fields.blocks/5/text: Test it in a live debate: take two real ideas from the backlog and try to reject one by referencing the vision. If it doesn't work out, the wording needs to be rewritten.
fields.blocks/5/title: A vision without rejections is presentation decor
fields.blocks/6/text: Vision does not replace strategy and does not tell you what to do in a quarter. It sets the frame within which strategy chooses the path and goals set the immediate step.
